excerpt: Hebbia builds AI agents for investors, bankers and lawyers that work through large sets of documents. Its products Matrix and Max, funding, pricing and alternatives.
content:
Hebbia makes AI software for finance and professional-services firms. Its tools read and analyse large collections of documents, such as filings, earnings transcripts, data-room files and contracts, and turn them into structured answers and deliverables. Its homepage describes the platform as purpose-built AI trusted by investors, bankers, lawyers, consultants and Fortune 500 companies, and its solution pages cover investing, investment banking, legal and corporate finance.

Products

Hebbia sells two main products. Matrix is laid out as a grid: each row is a company or document and each column a question or research field, such as financials, leverage, shareholders or leadership changes, and AI agents fill in every cell and can produce slide-style outputs. Max, which Hebbia pitches as an AI analyst for deal teams, is a shared workspace where a team's AI work across thousands of files can be reused across the firm. Both connect to sources including SEC filings, earnings transcripts, FactSet, S&P Capital IQ, PitchBook, Preqin, SharePoint, Box, Salesforce and Snowflake. Logos on Hebbia's site include Morgan Stanley, MetLife, Centerview, New Mountain Capital and Latham & Watkins.

Founder and funding

Hebbia was founded by George Sivulka, its CEO, who started it while studying for a PhD in electrical engineering at Stanford, according to TechCrunch. In July 2024 it raised a $130 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Index Ventures, Google Ventures and Peter Thiel also investing. TechCrunch reported a valuation of roughly $700 million and, citing a person with knowledge of the matter, said Hebbia had $13 million of annual recurring revenue and was profitable when it pitched investors; Sivulka declined to comment on revenue or profitability. Index Ventures wrote at the time that Hebbia's revenue had grown 15 times in 18 months and that, according to its founder, it was used by 30% of the top 50 asset managers by assets under management.

Pricing

Hebbia does not publish prices. Its website offers a demo request rather than self-serve sign-up, so pricing is agreed with its sales team.

We have not tested Hebbia ourselves. This page brings together Hebbia's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.
